newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent edges higher on good technical support.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent edges higher on good technical support.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were firmer on Wednesday because of technical factors and following the release on Wednesday of modestly bullish weekly U.S. inventory data, brokers and traders said.
May Brent was 26 cents a barrel firmer at 1231 GMT and stood at $18.19. April gas oil, which expires on Thursday, was $1.25 a tonne up at $164.00 and May gas oil was also $1.25 up, at $165.
"There is nothing new here," one IPE broker said. "It is a technical market and there is a perception that the market is not as bearish as people had earlier expected.
"The scenario for gas oil is much the same."

Latest weekly data from the American Patroleum Institute (API) showed a weekly crude oil stockbuild in the U.S. of around a million barrels, while distillates and gasoline were respectively 1.0 million and 1.2 million barrels down on the week.
While crude and distillate stocks are each nine or ten million barrels above year-ago levels, gasoline inventories are 5.8 million barrels down from this time last year.
"Overall the figures are slightly positive, led by the strength of gasoline demand," GNI research said in a daily report.
"In the short term the fundamentals do look a little better."

Physical crude traders said a strong recovery in refining margins and arbitrage business to the U.S. had boosted dated Brent markets. An 18-20 Brent cargo traded at May Brent -82 cents, 10 cents above a deal on Tuesday.
